# jenkins_plugin (Resource)

Manages a Jenkins plugin through the update center, so plugin prerequisites can be
declared as code instead of installed by hand.

Installation is idempotent: if the plugin is already present at the requested version
(or at any version, when `version` is unset) no install is attempted. Some plugins
require a Jenkins restart before they become active; when that happens `pending_restart`
is set and a warning is emitted. Dependency plugins that Jenkins installs automatically
are left unmanaged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Install (or adopt) a plugin, pinning its version.
resource "jenkins_plugin" "git" {
  name    = "git"
  version = "5.2.0"
}

# Track the latest available version (drift-prone) and uninstall on destroy.
resource "jenkins_plugin" "vault" {
  name                 = "hashicorp-vault-plugin"
  uninstall_on_destroy = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The short name of the plugin to manage (e.g. `git`). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `uninstall_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether destroying the resource uninstalls the plugin from Jenkins. Defaults to `false`, which only drops the plugin from Terraform state and leaves it installed.
- `version` (String) The plugin version to install (e.g. `5.2.0`). When omitted, the latest available version is installed and this attribute reflects the installed version. Leaving it unset is drift-prone: Jenkins may install or already have a newer version than any previously recorded.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the plugin is currently active (loaded) in Jenkins.
- `id` (String) The short name of the plugin, which is also its unique identifier.
- `pending_restart` (Boolean) Whether Jenkins must be restarted before the plugin becomes active. When `true`, a warning diagnostic is emitted.
